question: What is the main reason we practice sharps safety in the ward?

options.A: To comply only with hospital dress codes
options.B: To prevent accidental injuries and infections
options.C: To reduce the cost of hospital equipment
options.D: To speed up the administration of injections

explanation: Sharps safety is all about keeping you and your patients safe from accidental cuts and punctures. You've got this! [learn more](GST114_U2_T8#GST114_U2_T8_h1)

question: Why is careless handling of needles and blades such a big deal in the hospital?

options.A: It damages expensive hospital instruments quickly
options.B: It causes patients to lose trust in the nursing staff
options.C: It can transmit dangerous infections to anyone nearby
options.D: It leads to immediate disciplinary action by management

explanation: A used sharp can easily pass germs straight into the bloodstream through a break in the skin. Always handle with care! [learn more](GST114_U2_T8#GST114_U2_T8_h1)

question: Which of these items is counted as a medical sharp?
explanation: Surgical blades have sharp edges that can easily cut human skin, so they belong in the sharps box. [learn more](GST114_U2_T8#GST114_U2_T8_h2)

question: Why do we treat broken glass ampoules with the same care as needles?

options.A: They dissolve quickly inside standard trash bins
options.B: They are made from recycled hospital plastics
options.C: They contain live viral vaccines inside them
options.D: They can easily puncture skin and cause deep cuts

explanation: Any broken glass with a sharp edge can cut you and introduce nasty germs. Treat them like needles! [learn more](GST114_U2_T8#GST114_U2_T8_h2)

question: Which bloodborne infection has the highest risk of spreading after just one accidental needle-stick?
explanation: Hepatitis B is super infectious and carries the highest transmission risk after a needle prick. Another reason to be extra careful! [learn more](GST114_U2_T8#GST114_U2_T8_h3)

question: A nurse accidentally pricks her finger with a hollow needle used to draw blood. What is the biggest worry?

options.A: Suffering from severe immediate muscle spasms
options.B: Developing an acute allergic reaction to latex
options.C: Developing localized skin necrosis on the finger
options.D: Exposure to bloodborne pathogens like HIV and Hepatitis

explanation: Hollow needles often hold infected blood inside them, which is why a prick poses a direct threat of viral transmission. [learn more](GST114_U2_T8#GST114_U2_T8_h3)

question: What is a very common cause of accidental needle-stick injuries during a busy shift?
explanation: Trying to put the cap back on a used needle with two hands is a recipe for a missed cap and a finger prick. Never recap! [learn more](GST114_U2_T8#GST114_U2_T8_h4)

question: Why should you never point a used sharp device toward your own body?

options.A: It causes the medication inside to evaporate quickly
options.B: It makes the needle dull for future patients
options.C: It increases the chance of a direct puncture injury
options.D: It violates hospital rules regarding uniform neatness

explanation: Keep sharp points facing away from you so that if your hand slips, you won't get poked. [learn more](GST114_U2_T8#GST114_U2_T8_h4)

question: When should you close a sharps container and switch it for a new one?

options.A: Only at the end of every calendar month
options.B: When the outside label begins to fade
options.C: When it reaches about three-quarters full
options.D: When it is completely overflowing at the top

explanation: Stopping at the three-quarter mark keeps items from sticking out of the top and poking someone. Safety first! [learn more](GST114_U2_T8#GST114_U2_T8_h5)

question: Where is the best spot to place a sharps container in the treatment room?

options.A: Underneath the sink in the staff breakroom
options.B: Inside a locked storage room down the hall
options.C: High up on a shelf outside patient reach
options.D: As close as possible to where procedures occur

explanation: Having the box right beside you means you never have to walk across the room carrying a used needle. [learn more](GST114_U2_T8#GST114_U2_T8_h5)

question: What is the correct step to take the moment a sharps container hits its fill line?

options.A: Leave the lid open for the next shift to use
options.B: Press the contents down firmly with your hand
options.C: Lock the lid securely and prepare for disposal
options.D: Empty the contents into a regular black bin

explanation: Locking the lid right away stops accidental spills and keeps protruding needles from injuring anyone. [learn more](GST114_U2_T8#GST114_U2_T8_h6)

question: Why is pressing down on the trash inside a sharps container a big no-no?

options.A: It breaks the plastic base and causes leaks
options.B: It ruins the color of the biohazard symbol
options.C: It causes the container to emit bad odors
options.D: It risks puncturing your hand through the debris

explanation: Pushing down on the contents forces hidden needles upward, straight into your fingers and palms. Never do it! [learn more](GST114_U2_T8#GST114_U2_T8_h6)

question: What is the very first thing you should do if you accidentally get poked by a needle?

options.A: Take a strong dose of broad antibiotics
options.B: Apply a tight tourniquet above the elbow
options.C: Fill out an incident report form for HR
options.D: Wash the puncture site with soap and water

explanation: Quickly washing the spot with soap and water helps flush away germs before they can enter your bloodstream. [learn more](GST114_U2_T8#GST114_U2_T8_h7)

question: Why must a needle-stick injury be reported to the infection control team right away?

options.A: To prove that the nurse was not paying attention to work
options.B: To make sure the patient gets charged extra hospital fees
options.C: To schedule a mandatory disciplinary hearing for the ward
options.D: To ensure quick medical review and timely post-exposure treatment

explanation: Medicines to prevent infection work best when taken within hours, so reporting it fast is super important for your health. [learn more](GST114_U2_T8#GST114_U2_T8_h7)

question: Which color of waste bin is standard for infectious medical waste like sharps in Nigeria?
explanation: Yellow is the universal and local color code for biohazardous and infectious medical waste. You'll see this everywhere in the wards! [learn more](GST114_U2_T8#GST114_U2_T8_h8)

question: What is the main purpose of infection control rules in Nigerian hospitals?

options.A: To ensure that patients clean their own rooms after surgery
options.B: To establish clear standards that protect staff and patients from harm
options.C: To limit the purchase of expensive imported medical equipment
options.D: To reduce the number of nursing shifts required in each ward

explanation: Hospital policies are there to guide safe habits and keep everyone—both nurses and patients—free from avoidable infections. [learn more](GST114_U2_T8#GST114_U2_T8_h8)
